newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha reiterates call for Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Berisha reiterates call for Albania force.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha voiced fresh support on Friday for a multinational force to protect relief supplies to his chaotic nation and said he believed it would not face wide opposition in the Balkan state.

Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, a Dutch diplomat leading a mission of European relief experts to Albania, told reporters after meeting Berisha: "We asked him if he thought it (a foreign force) was useful and he did."

Members of the U.N. Security Council met informally in New York on Thursday to consider a request from Italy to authorise a force to help pull the former communist state back from the brink of anarchy.
Berisha "thought that the majority of the people would have no problem with this", d'Ansembourg said. "Some people might but he did not expect this to lead to difficult situations."

D'Ansembourg, whose mission includes European Union representatives and experts from the OSCE security group and the Council of Europe, said he understood the U.N. would meet "again in New York on Monday or Tuesday on the issue of a security presence here".

He said that it was realistic to expect a U.N. decision by the end of next week. Albania urged quick action after more than 100 people died in turmoil since protests against failed pyramid savings schemes spilled over into an insurrection in early March.
